news.title: ‘Enormous stain on football’: FIFA boss attacks WC critics in ‘world class tantrum’
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has unloaded on critics of the World Cup, accusing the media of spread false narratives and hailing the recently concluded tournament as a raging success. In a stunning 887-word, 15-part rant posted on Instagram, Infantino added several more astonishing quotes to his already extensive catalogue as he addressed several of the big issues that arose during the World Cup held in the United States, Canada and Mexico. Get all the latest football news, highlights and analysis delivered straight to your inbox with Fox Sports Sportmail. Infantino stunned the world before the 2022 World Cup in Qatar when he addressed human rights concerns in staggering fashion during a press conference in Doha.

news.title: John Stones set for Inter move after shining for England at World Cup
news.lede: Defender left Manchester City on free transfer. ‘I still feel I have so much to give to a club’. Inter are closing in on signing John Stones as a free transfer after the 32-year-old defender left Manchester City in June. Inter and their rival Italian club Juventus were interested in Stones before the World Cup and the Nerazzurri are now in pole position to recruit him following his impressive form in England’s run to the semi-finals.

news.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino accuses critics of spreading hate at World Cup
news.lede: Infantino claims critics of World Cup ‘missed it all’. He again defends Balogun affair and treatment of Iran. The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has launched an extraordinary attack at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives, while defending the tournament as a success that celebrated unity, safety and inclusion. In a 15-part message published on Monday on Instagram, Infantino claimed detractors had overlooked the joy and togetherness experienced by millions of people around the world who witnessed the tournament, won by Spain and staged in the US, Canada and Mexico.

news.title: Vozinha Joins Colo-Colo After World Cup Breakthrough Draws Global Attention
news.lede: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha has joined Chilean club Colo-Colo after his performances at the 2026 FIFA World Cup attracted international attention. Colo-Colo president Anibal Mosa confirmed the agreement, bringing the 40-year-old to South America for the first time after he became a free agent upon leaving Portuguese club Chaves. The club has not disclosed the financial terms or the length of the contract. The transfer follows a World Cup in which the veteran goalkeeper established himself as one of the tournament’s most recognizable players through a series of decisive performances against higher-ranked opponents.

news.title: 'Sorry you were so consumed by hate' - Gianni Infantino blasts FIFA critics after 'most outstanding' World Cup
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has hit back at his detractors in extraordinary fashion, claiming that those who criticised the 2026 World Cup were "consumed by hate." In a lengthy and defiant statement, the head of world football’s governing body defended the tournament’s legacy and urged his opponents to "meditate or pray" instead of spreading negativity. In the wake of a tournament that was as much defined by its off-field drama as its on-field heroics, Infantino has chosen to go on the offensive. The FIFA president used his personal Instagram and the organisation’s official channels to deliver a stinging rebuke to the journalists and critics who questioned the logistics and integrity of the 2026 World Cup across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

news.title: FIFA WORLD CUP 2026: Cabral’s Wonder Strike for Cape Verde Crowned Best Goal of the 2026 World Cup
news.lede: Sidny Lopes Cabral’s breathtaking long-range effort for Cape Verde against Argentina has officially been voted the best goal of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, sealing its place in football history. The goal came in the Round of 32 when Cabral produced something fearless. Picking up the ball at distance, he unleashed a curling strike that bent through the air with precision and power, leaving the goalkeeper stranded and the crowd in disbelief. It was the kind of goal that doesn’t just win matches, it defines tournaments.

news.title: Gianni Infantino requested to appear before House Committee over Donald Trump relationship after World Cup chaos
news.lede: Jamie Raskin, the ranking member on the House Committee, has requested that the FIFA chief be scrutinised over his relationship with president Donald Trump. During the 2026 World Cup this summer, questions were raised around Infantino and Trump amid multiple controversies. The US president admitted that he had called the FIFA boss to overturn Folarin Balogun's suspension for their last-16 game. FIFA then went on to announce Balogun was free to play against Belgium for the USA, with his ban suspended following an shock change of protocol.
